phrase: Impact crater — a circular depression, often with a raised rim, formed by meteorite impact.
source_title: Impact cratering : a geologic process
justification: This phrase directly describes the visual shape of a crater as a circular depression with a raised rim, which would be visible in a photograph.

phrase: dark gray to slightly red materials (often represented as blue or black pixels in HRSC color images), found in the patera floors and topographic lows throughout the CHVP, have a basaltic composition
source_title: The Circum-Hellas Volcanic Province, Mars: Overview
justification: This phrase describes the color appearance (dark gray to slightly red, appearing blue or black in images) and spatial context (patera floors and topographic lows) of the dark basaltic material, directly characterizing what it looks like visually.

phrase: dark materials, comprised of sand sheets, extend even farther downwind
source_title: North polar region of Mars: Advances in stratigraphy, structure, and erosional modification
justification: This mentions dark materials and their spatial extent but does not describe the visual appearance (shape, texture, color, size) of dark dunes specifically.

phrase: a section of dark, sand-rich and light-toned ice-rich irregularly-bedded sequences
source_title: North polar region of Mars: Advances in stratigraphy, structure, and erosional modification
justification: This describes stratigraphic sequences with dark and sand-rich characteristics but refers to subsurface units rather than the visual appearance of dunes in imagery.

phrase: Polyhydrated sulfates, that match any Ca-, Na-, Fe-, or Mg-sulfates with more than one water molecule, are preferentially present on less eroded and darker outcrops than outcrops of kieserite.
source_title: Spectral and geological study of the sulfate-rich region of West Candor Chasma, Mars
justification: This describes outcrops of sulfates, not the visual appearance of dark dunes themselves.

phrase: Pyroxenes are present mainly on sand dunes in the low lying terrains.
source_title: Spectral and geological study of the sulfate-rich region of West Candor Chasma, Mars
justification: This mentions dunes only in passing as a location for pyroxene minerals, without describing what the dunes look like visually.

phrase: Small, bright dune forms lie stratigraphically beneath the large dark dune field.
source_title: Aeolian processes in Proctor Crater on Mars: Sedimentary history as analyzed from multiple data sets
justification: This phrase describes the dark dune field's visual context by contrasting its large scale and dark tone against smaller, bright dune forms beneath it.

phrase: large reversing transverse and star dunes that dominate the dune field
source_title: Aeolian processes in Proctor Crater on Mars: Sedimentary history as analyzed from multiple data sets
justification: This phrase describes the visual shape and morphology of the dark dunes, specifying their forms as reversing transverse and star dunes.

phrase: Spectral deconvolution indicates that the dark dunes have infrared spectra consistent with basalt-like materials.
source_title: Aeolian processes in Proctor Crater on Mars: Sedimentary history as analyzed from multiple data sets
justification: This describes compositional properties measured instrumentally, not the visual appearance of the dunes in a photograph.

phrase: The dark dunes have both active slip faces and seemingly inactive slip faces
source_title: Aeolian processes in Proctor Crater on Mars: Sedimentary history as analyzed from multiple data sets
justification: This describes a visible structural feature of the dark dunes — their slip faces — which are directly observable in imagery.

phrase: Light-toned bed forms investigated at Gusev are coarse-grained ripples, an interpretation we propose for many of the smallest linear, light-toned bed forms of uncertain origin seen in high-resolution orbital images across Mars.
source_title: Wind-driven particle mobility on Mars: Insights from Mars Exploration Rover observations at ``El Dorado'' and surroundings at Gusev Crater
justification: This describes light-toned bedforms, not dark dunes, and focuses on interpretation rather than visual appearance of dark dunes.

phrase: active mafic sand ripples and larger inactive coarse-grained ripples interact
source_title: Wind-driven particle mobility on Mars: Insights from Mars Exploration Rover observations at ``El Dorado'' and surroundings at Gusev Crater
justification: This mentions mafic (dark) sand ripples in passing as part of a activity description, without describing their visual appearance such as shape, color, or texture in detail.

phrase: These recurring slope lineae are narrow, dark markings on steep slopes that appear and incrementally lengthen during warm seasons on low-albedo surfaces.
source_title: Recurring slope lineae in equatorial regions of Mars
justification: This describes recurring slope lineae (RSL), a phenomenon explicitly distinct from slope_streak per the class description, so it does not describe the slope_streak class's visual appearance.

phrase: the resolution of at least one splotch into an extensive dune system
source_title: Variable features in Mars: Preliminary Mariner 9 Television Results (A 4. 1)
justification: This phrase mentions a dune system but does not describe its visual appearance such as shape, texture, color, or size in any meaningful way.

phrase: bright and dark linear streaks, generally emanating from craters
source_title: Variable features in Mars: Preliminary Mariner 9 Television Results (A 4. 1)
justification: This describes streaks rather than bright dunes specifically, and only notes their linear shape and association with craters, not dune visual characteristics.

phrase: Transverse aeolian ridges (TARs) are small bright windblown deposits found throughout the Martian tropics that stand a few meters tall and are spaced a few tens of meters apart.
source_title: The birth and death of transverse aeolian ridges on Mars
justification: This sentence directly describes the visual and physical appearance of bright dune-like features (TARs), including their brightness, small size (few meters tall), and spacing (few tens of meters apart).

phrase: The south polar residual cap (SPRC) includes sublimation pits, the so-called Swiss Cheese terrains".
source_title: Temporal and Geographical evolution of the South Pole CO2-Ice Sublimation Pits
justification: This phrase names the visual class and its geologic context but does not describe its shape, texture, color, or size.

phrase: SPRC pits have been observed to grow with time and represent one stage of the Martian CO2 cycle in which CO2 ice mass is returned to the atmosphere through seasonal sublimation during the southern hemisphere summer.
source_title: Temporal and Geographical evolution of the South Pole CO2-Ice Sublimation Pits
justification: This describes the process and temporal behavior of the pits, not their visual appearance in an image.

phrase: beneath the conformal coating of seasonal ice, radially-organized channels are connected in spidery patterns
source_title: HiRISE observations of gas sublimation-driven activity in Mars’ southern polar regions: I. Erosion of the surface
justification: This phrase directly describes the visual appearance of spider terrain as radially-organized channels connected in spidery (branching, radial) patterns beneath ice.

phrase: Dark fans of material from the substrate are observed draped over the seasonal ice, and this material collects in thin to thick layers in the channels
source_title: HiRISE observations of gas sublimation-driven activity in Mars’ southern polar regions: I. Erosion of the surface
justification: This describes the visual appearance of the spider features in HiRISE images, including the dark fan deposits visible on the surface draped over ice and collecting in the channels.

phrase: southern radially-organized channels ("araneiform" terrain)
source_title: Observations of the northern seasonal polar cap on Mars: I. Spring sublimation activity and processes
justification: This phrase describes the visual appearance of araneiform (spider) terrain as radially-organized channels, indicating the branching, spoke-like spatial arrangement visible in images.

phrase: The newly detected dendritic troughs are small shallow branching troughs (≈ 1.4 m wide) similar to the seasonal furrows previously detected in the northern hemisphere
source_title: Present-day erosion of Martian polar terrain by the seasonal CO<SUB>2</SUB> jets
justification: This phrase describes the physical appearance of the troughs — small, shallow, and branching — providing size and morphological detail visible in imagery.

phrase: their overall geometry turns from linear to dendritic, a characteristic shared with araneiform terrains
source_title: Present-day erosion of Martian polar terrain by the seasonal CO<SUB>2</SUB> jets
justification: This describes the visual geometry of the features, noting the branching dendritic shape that characterizes the spider-like araneiform appearance.

phrase: features with a central pit and radiating channels known as 'spiders'
source_title: Planet Four: Terrains - Discovery of araneiforms outside of the South Polar layered deposits
justification: This phrase directly describes the visual morphology of spiders as having a central pit with channels radiating outward from it.

phrase: These deposits originate from araneiform structures (spiders), boulders on ridges, cracks on slopes, and along linear cracks in the slab ice on flatter surfaces.
source_title: HiRISE observations of gas sublimation-driven activity in Mars’ southern polar regions: II. Surficial deposits and their origins
justification: This phrase names araneiform structures as sources of deposits but does not describe their visual appearance such as shape, texture, color, or size.

phrase: a typically rocky and red Martian landscape at last light
source_title: Gamesman Problems
justification: This phrase describes the visual context of the Martian horizon scene, including the color (red), terrain texture (rocky), and lighting condition (last light) visible in such an image.

phrase: Earth as a bright evening star, grouped with Jupiter and Venus, hanging low above a typically rocky and red Martian landscape at last light
source_title: Gamesman Problems
justification: This sentence describes the visual appearance of a Mars horizon scene, depicting what is visible above the skyline including celestial objects hanging low above the landscape.
